preface.title: Preface
preface.para: ooRexx/Python is a bridge between Open Object Rexx and Python 3, both ways: an ooRexx program uses Python modules as Rexx objects, and a Python program runs Rexx code and uses Rexx objects as Python objects. This book shows how, through short programs, each showing one thing.

Every recipe is one of the samples that come with the bridge: the program, the Python it replaces, how to run it, what it prints, and what happens. The book is made from the samples themselves, and every sample is run, and its output checked, with every Python from 3.9 on, on Linux, macOS and Windows, so what the book says a program prints is what it prints.

The book is for ooRexx programmers who want Python's libraries, and for Python programmers who want Rexx. It is not long: read the first three chapters, then whichever recipe you need. Each recipe ends with the place in ooRexx and Python: Reference that has the details.

section.title: The Samples
section.para: The samples are in the samples folder of the project's repository, and the installer copies them into ooRexx's samples folder, under python. Their names start with a number: 01 to 27 are ooRexx using Python, 30 to 34 Python using ooRexx. Python's output (a list, a float) is shown as Python prints it.
